Upgrade

Keep translation automatic

The ≈ line is Google Translate: instant. The ✦ line is an AI. It reads the surrounding conversation, so slang and replies come out right. Your first 7 days are free and fully automatic, with ≈ and ✦ on every message in another language. After that, a free install translates a message when you click ≈ Translate under it. If Google may have misread a message, its line says ≈ rough, and you also see the start of the ✦ line, up to 3 times a day. Paying keeps everything automatic.

The checkout page does not show your code. Dodo Payments emails it to you, with the subject "Your License Key is Ready". That license key is your Subline code. Check spam.

New install: paste it in the installer. Already installed: in Discord, open User Settings, then Plugins (under Vencord). Open the settings of VcTranslate. Paste the key in Subline Code. That makes everything automatic.

Installing

The security warning

On a Mac, Subline is signed and checked by Apple, so macOS only asks once if you want to open it. The Windows build isn't code-signed yet. I haven't paid for a certificate, so Windows shows a warning the first time. It's the unknown-developer warning, not a malware detection. Here are the steps.

On a Mac

  1. Open the .dmg and drag Subline to Applications.

    If macOS later says Subline is not supported on this Mac, you have an Intel Mac. Download the Intel version instead.

  2. Open Subline from Applications.

    macOS asks once"Subline" is an app downloaded from the internet. Are you sure you want to open it?

    Click Open.

  3. Follow Subline's screens.

    Click Continue. If Discord is open, click Quit Discord for me. Pick the language you read.

  4. Paste your code, or skip it.

    Bought a plan? Paste the code from the Dodo Payments email and click Save code. Check spam. No code? Click Continue without a code. Your first 7 days are still free and automatic.

  5. Turn on Subline.

    Click Continue. System Settings opens. Turn Subline on under App Management. If macOS asks to quit Subline, choose Later. Subline waits for you and carries on by itself. Closed that window? Click Open it again.

  6. Discord opens with Subline.

    Messages in other languages get a translation under them.

On Windows

  1. Keep the download.

    Your browser may saySubline-Setup isn't commonly downloaded.

    In Edge, click ... next to the file, then Keep. Then click Show more, then Keep anyway. In Chrome, click Keep.

  2. Open the Subline-Setup file you downloaded.

    Windows saysWindows protected your PC.

    Click More info, then Run anyway.

  3. Click Install, then Finish.

    Leave Run Subline ticked. Subline opens.

  4. Follow Subline's screens.

    Click Continue. If Discord is open, click Quit Discord for me. Pick the language you read.

  5. Paste your code, or skip it.

    Bought a plan? Paste the code from the Dodo Payments email and click Save code. Check spam. No code? Click Continue without a code. Your first 7 days are still free and automatic. Subline then opens Discord.

Privacy

Where your messages go

Translating means sending text somewhere. Here's exactly where.

WhatGoes whereStored?
Message textGoogle for the instant ≈ line. For the ✦ line, Subline's own relay gets the message and a few messages before it. It sends them to OpenRouter, which runs the AI on Groq or a similar host, and returns the translation. If OpenRouter fails, the relay sends them straight to Groq.No. The relay stores no message text. It keeps counts only.
Who sent itFor the ✦ line, the sender's Discord username goes to the relay with the text, so the AI can tell who said what. If a message mentions a person, channel, or role, that name goes as part of the text, to Google and the relay. Avatars and server names are never sent.No.
Your Subline codeAn access token that unlocks the ✦ AI. No name, email, or personal info is attached. It goes to the relay only when you translate.A usage count, nothing more.
Free install idFree installs send a random id when Discord starts and with each free ✦. It times your 7 free days and counts your 3 free ✦ previews a day. It is not tied to your name or account. Each free ✦ also counts your IP address, to limit abuse.A usage count per id and per IP address. The IP address count is deleted after 2 days. The time the id was first seen is kept, so its 7 free days cannot restart.
Usage dataThe Discord app sends none. The relay keeps a count per code or free install id: how many translations, and whether they worked. No message text, no names.Counts only.
  • off
    DMs are off. A DM is never translated on its own. You can turn one on per conversation. Or press ⚡ on one message to translate it. That sends it and the few messages before it.
  • off
    Your own messages are never translated. If you read English, Subline skips text it is sure is English before sending anything. Everything else goes to Google, which skips what is already in your language. After a free trial ends, only the messages you click go. With ✦ on, a few recent messages, yours included, go to the relay as context.
  • you
    Turn it off. To stop one channel, hover over a message in it and click the globe button, labeled Disable auto-translate here. Click it again to turn the channel back on. To stop every server channel, switch off Global Auto in the VcTranslate plugin settings. After that, only channels you turn on with the globe button translate.

Subline is an independent project. The source is on GitHub. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Discord. It's a client modification you install yourself. Use it at your own discretion.
